title: Qt: Enforce Minimum Qt version 5.11
description:
We already strongly recommend Qt version 5.12 and enforce 5.10.
Commit 06cd84a6e9f8bd0807cca35595b94b07de254b07 said "[a]lthough
build support for 5.10 and 5.11 is not being removed at this point,
it might be for 4.x at a later time."
    
Move to enforcing 5.11, and update macos-setup for that as well.
Remove the QT_VERSION_CHECKs for 5.10 and 5.11 (except in
qcustomplot.)

Hold off on enforcing 5.12 for now, because there isn't any code
that needs 5.12 or greater (there are two places for a workaround
for Qt 5.12.0 through 5.12.5), and because Debian Buster is on
Qt 5.11.3. There are not any known supported OS distributions on
Qt 5.10.

notes.body: No. This will break builds for RHEL versions, which are still required for some companies. As much as I am for moving up in this regards, we only recently changed the version and we should stick with it at least for this year. I am strongly opposed in changing the minimum version twice within 6 months just for convenience and not due to technical necessity.

I certainly agree with not breaking the build for RHEL version, but what version are you talking about?

RHEL8 with all updates is on Qt 5.15. Even the initial release of RHEL 8.0 was [Qt 5.11.1](https://vault.centos.org/8.0.1905/AppStream/x86_64/os/Packages/), which is another reason (like Debian buster) to enforce only to Qt 5.11.

For RHEL7, 4.0 (much less master) cannot be built anyway because of other requirements, such as the c-ares version, gnutls, and libgcrypt.

It was raised the last time around as well. I just don't think this is the right call that close to already raising the minimum. We have to provide a stable interface, and if that means that we keep older versions around for a while, so be it. Qt 5.9 is still around, and RHEL 5.x and 6.x are still being used in production. Now, I agree in general that we should move to newer versions, just we have already raised the version with 4.0 and I see no point to raising it again with 4.2. I would much rather raise it, when we come to 4.4 or 4.6 as it is more time in between. To be totally honest, I would actually avoid raising it for such an integral part until 5.x, as it will lead to issues.

https://access.redhat.com/support/policy/updates/errata
RHEL 5.x,6.x and <=7.6 has reach EOM, no more software update will come. Regards RHEL 7.9 there is still Maintenance Support 2 ongoing until 30062024. However Maintenance support 2 state "New functionality and new hardware enablement are not planned" and in the "Red Hat Enterprise Linux Life Cycle" table it's noted Support 2 will only get minor version update of software, hence wireshark 4.x is not in the scope.

+# The minimum supported version of Qt is 5.11, so the minimum supported version
